currentContext.strengths: ~65% share of India's Natural Gas Transmission and ~48% share of the domestic Natural Gas Market|Diversified LNG portfolio of ~16.5 MMTPA sourced from the USA, Qatar, Australia and other geographies, positioning GAIL as one of the leading global LNG players|Largest CGD ecosystem in the country through subsidiaries/JVs - presence across 72 Geographical Areas, over one crore PNG consumers and 3,400+ CNG stations|Fully integrated business model spanning LNG sourcing, shipping, transmission, marketing and downstream petrochemicals, enabling agile response to supply disruptions|Largest supplier to India's Fertilizer sector (supplies ~two-thirds of sector gas consumption to 31 of 36 urea units) and ~45% of gas consumed by gas-based power plants|Active R&D and IP base: more than 30 collaborative research projects with premier institutions and an IP portfolio of 52 patents filed (40 granted) plus six registered copyrights
currentContext.strategies: Expand the gas-based economy in India in line with GoI's vision to raise the share of gas in the energy basket from ~6% to 15% by 2030|Diversify LNG sourcing (long-term contracts, spot cargoes, swap transactions) and expand own/chartered shipping capacity to optimise freight cost and mitigate price volatility|Pursue long-term LNG offtake/sale tie-ups with global producers and traders to meet growing downstream Indian gas demand|Diversify into the Polyester value chain via PTA production at wholly-owned subsidiary GAIL Mangalore Petrochemicals Limited (GMPL), and into Propylene via PDH technology at Usar|Strengthen digital transformation and operational excellence: SAP S/4HANA migration, Vendor Invoice Management Portal, Project Sanchay II for data-driven decision-making|Expand the National Gas Grid / pipeline network (~1,500 km further pipeline in execution) to widen reach to untapped markets and raise market share|Grow City Gas Distribution (CGD) presence in PNG/CNG segments through subsidiaries and JVs across Geographical Areas, targeting increased market share as the sector grows|Use newly incorporated GAIL Global IFSC Limited (GIFT City) for treasury management and to explore ship-leasing and international financial services|Pursue Steel-sector customers to substitute cooking coal with natural gas as new pipelines (JHBDPL, MNJPL) widen access in Eastern India|Remain the largest supplier to the Fertilizer sector, leveraging steady subsidised demand|As a Government Company, GAIL is exempt from Companies Act provisions on Directors' remuneration/appointment policy disclosure (Sections 178(3) and 197). Dividend pay-out follows the Company's Board-approved Dividend Distribution Policy adopted under SEBI LODR Regulation 43A. For FY 2025-26 the Board recommended a Final Dividend of 5% (Re 0.50 per equity share) on paid-up equity capital, in addition to an Interim Dividend already paid during the year, reflecting a policy of regular shareholder pay-outs alongside continued reinvestment in transmission, LNG, petrochemicals and pipeline expansion.
currentContext.expansion: GAIL's FY2025-26 expansion centred on natural gas pipeline build-out: ~2,000 km of pipeline was commissioned during the year, including large sections of the Mumbai-Nagpur-Jharsuguda Pipeline (MNJPL, ~1,504 of 1,707 km), the Srikakulam-Angul Pipeline (SAPL, ~470 of 744 km) and progress on the Kochi-Koottanad-Bengaluru-Mangaluru Phase II (KKBMPL-II) project in Tamil Nadu. A further ~1,500 km of gas pipeline projects remain under execution across multiple states (Kolkata-Haldia, Dhamra-Haldia, Nagpur-Jharsuguda, SAPL spurlines, KKBMPL-II, Gurdaspur-Jammu, DUPL-DPPL augmentation and various spur lines), which management is hopeful of completing within the current calendar year. On LNG infrastructure, the Dabhol (Konkan LNG) terminal now operates as an all-weather port and the Company plans to expand its regasification capacity from 5.0 MMTPA to 6.3 MMTPA in a first phase over the next three years. In petrochemicals, GAIL commissioned a 60 KTA Polypropylene unit at Pata (Feb 2026, taking the Pata complex to 870 KTA) and is building a 500 KTA Propane Dehydrogenation-Polypropylene (PDH-PP) plant at Usar (equipment delivered, construction in progress, commissioning targeted FY2027-28) - India's first plant to use PDH technology. Wholly-owned subsidiary GAIL Mangalore Petrochemicals Limited (GMPL) is commissioning a PTA plant (branded 'G-Tex') under a polyester-value-chain diversification. In LPG infrastructure, the Jamnagar-Loni Pipeline (JLPL) is being augmented from 3.25 MMTPA to 6.5 MMTPA (involving ~1,150 km of new pipeline and pumping-station upgrades), and GAIL has bid for three new PNGRB-tendered LPG pipelines. GAIL is also forward-integrating into fertilisers, with two proposed gas-based urea/ammonia plants planned along the MNJPL corridor to anchor pipeline demand, and broke ground on a new 30-acre R&D Centre at IMT Sohna, Haryana (land possession taken Feb 2026) to strengthen technology capability across core and emerging clean-energy areas.

risks.risk: Project execution delay risk - pipeline and process plant projects
risks.note: Management flags delay in execution of pipeline and process-plant projects as a Top Corporate Level Key Risk; large ongoing projects (MNJPL, SAPL, KKBMPL-II, PDH-PP Usar, GMPL PTA) carry commissioning-timeline risk.

risks.risk: Underutilization of the Natural Gas pipeline asset base
risks.note: Listed as a Top Corporate Level Key Risk; the Company's own five-year data shows Natural Gas Transmission installed capacity utilisation moving in a range, reflecting demand/off-take variability against a large fixed pipeline network.

risks.risk: Restructuring risk - monetization/unbundling of pipeline assets
risks.note: Explicitly flagged as a Top Corporate Level Key Risk; potential regulatory-driven unbundling or monetisation of GAIL's pipeline network could alter its integrated business model and asset ownership.

Adverse movement of crude oil/LNG prices, shortage of LNG cargoes, an expected increase in domestic gas volumes, and risk of LNG contract default by upstream suppliers are flagged; GAIL largely imports LNG, capital goods and stores & spares, adding foreign-exchange exposure that is managed under its Foreign Currency & Interest Rate Risk Management Policy and Commodity Price Risk Management (CPRM) Policy.

Risk of reduced Petrochemical margins from higher imports, lower prices and high input costs; specific risk of unviable operations at the Pata plant due to higher feedstock cost, and at the Pata/Vijaipur C2-C3 plant due to reduced availability of C2-C3 in feed gas.

Flagged risks include reduction of APM (Administered Price Mechanism) gas allocation, decrease in market share of domestic gas, inability to acquire new volumes of domestic gas, and shutdown of ONGC facilities that supply feed gas.

risks.risk: Pipeline/plant safety and third-party damage risk
risks.note: Explosion or high-fatality leakage risk is flagged across LPG & NG pipelines and their RT/SV stations, Petrochemical and GPU/C2-C3 recovery plants, and CGD NG pipelines, alongside risk of third-party damage and encroachment and broader natural/man-made calamity risk (blowout, earthquake, tsunami, terrorism); mitigated via design standards, an Emergency Response and Disaster Management Plan, and a Mega Insurance/Large Risk Insurance policy.
Management flags inadequate controls to protect systems against malicious attacks as a Top Corporate Level Key Risk, which could result in loss of data and disruption of operations.

themes.title: Oil & Gas - gas economy (CGD/LNG) + refining/upstream
themes.need: India's gas-economy push now collides with an outright policy reversal. ATGL grew volume 13% to 303 MMSCM and revenue 27% to INR 1,908cr, yet EBITDA FELL sequentially to INR 281cr (~14.7% margin, from INR 310cr) because the government withdrew the pooled-gas mechanism after the West Asia 'peace deal', pushing ATGL to ~15% spot volumes with Brent above $107/bbl; management also noted NWG price is 12% of the Indian crude basket, so a 62% domestic mix protects far less than it looks, and CNG station adds slowed to +5 from +25 in Q4 even as CNG demand grows ~30%. The same shock ran the other way for integrated refining: RELIANCE delivered O2C EBITDA of INR 17,000cr (+17%) THROUGH the Strait-of-Hormuz closure at 96-97% throughput while Asian peers ran 15-20% below capacity, with ethane+ROGC at ~70% of ethylene feed as distillate cracks blew out (gas oil $16 to $63, ATF $14 to $62). MGL/GUJGASLTD/IGL/IRMENERGY carry the same CGD margin squeeze; PETRONET/OIL/ONGC/IOC ride LNG-infra + domestic-gas; CHENNPETRO/MRPL ride GRM cracks; DEEPINDS/JINDRILL/SEAMECLTD on ONGC E&P capex; AEGISLOG/AEGISVOPAK add LPG/gas terminalling.
themes.driver: Whether the pooled/APM gas-allocation mechanism is restored (the single biggest CGD earnings variable); LNG spot price and Brent; GRM/distillate cracks; ONGC rig tenders & day-rates.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Government of India's policy push to raise natural gas share in the energy mix from ~6% to 15% by 2030 is expected to structurally lift gas demand
- CGD sector is expected to grow at more than 10% CAGR, presenting future growth potential for PNG/CNG expansion
- Fertilizer sector demand expected to remain steady and GAIL expected to remain the largest supplier due to subsidy support on gas price
- Power-sector incremental demand met via competitive supply under the NVVN Scheme and Section 11 of the Electricity Act during supply-constrained periods
- Widening pipeline access (JHBDPL, MNJPL) in Eastern India is expected to enable Steel-sector customers to switch from cooking coal to natural gas
- Diversified domestic gas procurement (IGX platform, tenders, bilateral agreements) intended to improve availability and pricing for downstream customers
- ~1,500 km of additional Natural Gas pipeline projects at various stages of execution across the Country, including balance sections of MNJPL, SAPL and the KKBMPL-II (Singasadra-Krishnagiri) project in Tamil Nadu
- Progress table of approved pipeline projects as of March 2026: JHBDPL incl. Barauni-Guwahati (3,290 km total, 3,128 km commissioned), Kochi-Koottanad-Bengaluru-Mangaluru Phase II (902 km total, 608 km commissioned), Srikakulam-Angul (744 km total, 469.5 km commissioned), Dhamra-Haldia (253 km total, 154 km commissioned), Mumbai-Nagpur-Jharsuguda (1,707 km total, 1,504 km commissioned), Gurdaspur-Jammu (153 km total, not yet commissioned)
- Dabhol LNG terminal capacity expansion from 5.0 MMTPA to 6.3 MMTPA planned in the first phase over the next 3 years, subject to completion of the Ambient Air Heating System currently under construction
- Jamnagar-Loni LPG Pipeline (JLPL) capacity augmentation approved from 3.25 MMTPA to 6.5 MMTPA
- Bids submitted for three new PNGRB-tendered LPG pipelines: Cherlapally-Nagpur (~550 km), Jhansi-Sitarganj (~605 km) and Shikrapur to Goa & Hubli (~620 km)
- 500 KTA Propane Dehydrogenation and Polypropylene (PDH-PP) plant under execution at Usar, Maharashtra, expected commissioning FY 2027-28 - India's first plant using PDH technology for Propylene
- GAIL Mangalore Petrochemicals Ltd (GMPL) PTA plant nearing commissioning, with sub-system and system commissioning activities in progress

- As on 30th June 2026 (Standalone) the deck states Capital Employed of Rs. 105,910 crore, Net Worth of Rs. 70,658 crore and LT Loan Outstanding of Rs. 13,823 crore.
- Debt Equity Ratio is shown rising across the series: 0.22 (FY23), 0.29 (FY24), 0.26 (FY25), 0.28 (FY26) and 0.32 (Q1 FY27).
- Equity of Rs. 77,593 crore comprises Equity Share Capital of Rs. 6,575 crore and Other Equity of Rs. 71,018 crore, within which Retained Earnings are Rs. 63,956 crore.
- A footnote records that "Share Price & EPS for past periods are adjusted for Bonus issue & Buy Back", indicating both have occurred, though the deck gives no dates or amounts.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: GAIL's FY2025-26 expansion centred on natural gas pipeline build-out: ~2,000 km of pipeline was commissioned during the year, including large sections of the Mumbai-Nagpur-Jharsuguda Pipeline (MNJPL, ~1,504 of 1,707 km), the Srikakulam-Angul Pipeline (SAPL, ~470 of 744 km) and progress on the Kochi-Koottanad-Bengaluru-Mangaluru Phase II (KKBMPL-II) project in Tamil Nadu. A further ~1,500 km of gas pipeline projects remain under execution across multiple states (Kolkata-Haldia, Dhamra-Haldia, Nagpur-Jharsuguda, SAPL spurlines, KKBMPL-II, Gurdaspur-Jammu, DUPL-DPPL augmentation and various spur lines), which management is hopeful of completing within the current calendar year. On LNG infrastructure, the Dabhol (Konkan LNG) terminal now operates as an all-weather port and the Company plans to expand its regasification capacity from 5.0 MMTPA to 6.3 MMTPA in a first phase over the next three years. In petrochemicals, GAIL commissioned a 60 KTA Polypropylene unit at Pata (Feb 2026, taking the Pata complex to 870 KTA) and is building a 500 KTA Propane Dehydrogenation-Polypropylene (PDH-PP) plant at Usar (equipment delivered, construction in progress, commissioning targeted FY2027-28) - India's first plant to use PDH technology. Wholly-owned subsidiary GAIL Mangalore Petrochemicals Limited (GMPL) is commissioning a PTA plant (branded 'G-Tex') under a polyester-value-chain diversification. In LPG infrastructure, the Jamnagar-Loni Pipeline (JLPL) is being augmented from 3.25 MMTPA to 6.5 MMTPA (involving ~1,150 km of new pipeline and pumping-station upgrades), and GAIL has bid for three new PNGRB-tendered LPG pipelines. GAIL is also forward-integrating into fertilisers, with two proposed gas-based urea/ammonia plants planned along the MNJPL corridor to anchor pipeline demand, and broke ground on a new 30-acre R&D Centre at IMT Sohna, Haryana (land possession taken Feb 2026) to strengthen technology capability across core and emerging clean-energy areas.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- ~65% share of India's Natural Gas Transmission and ~48% share of the domestic Natural Gas Market
- Diversified LNG portfolio of ~16.5 MMTPA sourced from the USA, Qatar, Australia and other geographies, positioning GAIL as one of the leading global LNG players
- Largest CGD ecosystem in the country through subsidiaries/JVs - presence across 72 Geographical Areas, over one crore PNG consumers and 3,400+ CNG stations
- Fully integrated business model spanning LNG sourcing, shipping, transmission, marketing and downstream petrochemicals, enabling agile response to supply disruptions
- Largest supplier to India's Fertilizer sector (supplies ~two-thirds of sector gas consumption to 31 of 36 urea units) and ~45% of gas consumed by gas-based power plants
- Active R&D and IP base: more than 30 collaborative research projects with premier institutions and an IP portfolio of 52 patents filed (40 granted) plus six registered copyrights

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Project execution delay risk - pipeline and process plant projects — Management flags delay in execution of pipeline and process-plant projects as a Top Corporate Level Key Risk; large ongoing projects (MNJPL, SAPL, KKBMPL-II, PDH-PP Usar, GMPL PTA) carry commissioning-timeline risk.
- Underutilization of the Natural Gas pipeline asset base — Listed as a Top Corporate Level Key Risk; the Company's own five-year data shows Natural Gas Transmission installed capacity utilisation moving in a range, reflecting demand/off-take variability against a large fixed pipeline network.
- Restructuring risk - monetization/unbundling of pipeline assets — Explicitly flagged as a Top Corporate Level Key Risk; potential regulatory-driven unbundling or monetisation of GAIL's pipeline network could alter its integrated business model and asset ownership.
- LNG market and price risk — Adverse movement of crude oil/LNG prices, shortage of LNG cargoes, an expected increase in domestic gas volumes, and risk of LNG contract default by upstream suppliers are flagged; GAIL largely imports LNG, capital goods and stores & spares, adding foreign-exchange exposure that is managed under its Foreign Currency & Interest Rate Risk Management Policy and Commodity Price Risk Management (CPRM) Policy.
- Petrochemical margin and feedstock risk — Risk of reduced Petrochemical margins from higher imports, lower prices and high input costs; specific risk of unviable operations at the Pata plant due to higher feedstock cost, and at the Pata/Vijaipur C2-C3 plant due to reduced availability of C2-C3 in feed gas.
- Domestic Natural Gas business risk — Flagged risks include reduction of APM (Administered Price Mechanism) gas allocation, decrease in market share of domestic gas, inability to acquire new volumes of domestic gas, and shutdown of ONGC facilities that supply feed gas.
- Pipeline/plant safety and third-party damage risk — Explosion or high-fatality leakage risk is flagged across LPG & NG pipelines and their RT/SV stations, Petrochemical and GPU/C2-C3 recovery plants, and CGD NG pipelines, alongside risk of third-party damage and encroachment and broader natural/man-made calamity risk (blowout, earthquake, tsunami, terrorism); mitigated via design standards, an Emergency Response and Disaster Management Plan, and a Mega Insurance/Large Risk Insurance policy.
- Cybersecurity risk — Management flags inadequate controls to protect systems against malicious attacks as a Top Corporate Level Key Risk, which could result in loss of data and disruption of operations.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Expand the gas-based economy in India in line with GoI's vision to raise the share of gas in the energy basket from ~6% to 15% by 2030
- Diversify LNG sourcing (long-term contracts, spot cargoes, swap transactions) and expand own/chartered shipping capacity to optimise freight cost and mitigate price volatility
- Pursue long-term LNG offtake/sale tie-ups with global producers and traders to meet growing downstream Indian gas demand
- Diversify into the Polyester value chain via PTA production at wholly-owned subsidiary GAIL Mangalore Petrochemicals Limited (GMPL), and into Propylene via PDH …
